decisions.reason: As the direct successor to an earlier voltage-measurement module, it rests on strong accumulated electronics, firmware, and customer-use knowledge, so we can refine it efficiently and see little reason to withdraw it.

The MQTT proxy builds on our software, connectivity, and API capabilities and complements the modular platform, although as a software-side add-on it remains somewhat easier to discontinue than core hardware modules.
The CAN bus interface is close to our core competence in embedded communication and automation applications, giving us the knowledge base to support and improve it for industrial users.
A carbon dioxide sensor module fits directly into our sensing portfolio, where our existing hardware, firmware, documentation, and customer understanding make continued commercialization attractive.

The touch panel accessory is the most peripheral to our main sensing, control, and communication platform, so our ability to build cumulative learning and distinctive improvements around it is weaker than for the other products.
